title: Word Count Ranking
statement: You are given n words. Print each distinct word with the number of times it appears. Sort the lines by count, largest first. If two words have the same count, put them in alphabetical order. Words use only lowercase English letters, so alphabetical order is the normal dictionary order.
inputFormat: First line: integer n. Then n words, separated by spaces or new lines.
outputFormat: One line for each distinct word: the word, a space, then its count. Lines follow the sorting rule above.
constraints: Each word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters (a to z)
Words are separated by spaces or new lines
explanations: apple and banana both appear 2 times, so they are in alphabetical order. cherry appears once, so it comes last.
zebra appears 3 times, dog 2 times, cat once. Higher count comes first, so the order is zebra, dog, cat.
reference:
import sys
from collections import Counter

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
words = data[1:1 + n]
c = Counter(words)
for w, k in sorted(c.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0])):
    print(w, k)
